import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 2.22

by Sh. S. Kemkhadze

An abstract group-theoretic property $\Sigma$ is radical if, in every group $G$, the subgroup
$\Sigma(G)$ generated by all normal $\Sigma$-subgroups is itself a $\Sigma$-group. It is strongly
radical if it is radical and $G/\Sigma(G)$ has no nontrivial normal $\Sigma$-subgroups.

Is Kurosh's property $\overline{RN}$ radical? Is it strongly radical?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 2.22.
-/

namespace Kourovka.«2.22»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A complete chain of subgroups contains the supremum and infimum of each of its subfamilies.
In particular, taking the empty subfamily shows that it contains both $\bot$ and $\top$. -/
def IsCompleteSubgroupChain (S : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop :=
  IsChain (· ≤ ·) S ∧
    (∀ T : Set (Subgroup G), T ⊆ S → sSup T ∈ S) ∧
    (∀ T : Set (Subgroup G), T ⊆ S → sInf T ∈ S)

/-- The pair $A < B$ is a jump in a chain $S$ if no member of $S$ lies strictly between them. -/
def IsJump (S : Set (Subgroup G)) (A B : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  A ∈ S ∧ B ∈ S ∧ A < B ∧ ¬ ∃ C ∈ S, A < C ∧ C < B

/-- A normal system in $G$ is a complete chain of subgroups in which the lower member of every
jump is normal in the upper member. -/
def IsNormalSystem (S : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop :=
  IsCompleteSubgroupChain S ∧
    ∀ ⦃A B : Subgroup G⦄, IsJump S A B → (A.comap B.subtype).Normal

/-- A solvable normal system is a normal system all of whose factors are abelian. For a jump
$A < B$, abelianness of $B/A$ is expressed by $[B,B] \leq A$. -/
def IsSolvableNormalSystem (S : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop :=
  IsNormalSystem S ∧
    ∀ ⦃A B : Subgroup G⦄, IsJump S A B → ⁅B, B⁆ ≤ A

/-- Kurosh's class $\overline{RN}$ consists of the groups in which every normal system has a
refinement that is a solvable normal system. A refinement is represented by inclusion of the
corresponding complete chains. -/
def IsRNBarGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Set (Subgroup G), IsNormalSystem S →
    ∃ T : Set (Subgroup G), S ⊆ T ∧ IsSolvableNormalSystem T

/-- The $\overline{RN}$-radical candidate: the subgroup generated by all normal
$\overline{RN}$-subgroups. The normal closure does not enlarge their generated subgroup, since
all the subgroups in the union are normal. -/
def rnBarRadical (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.normalClosure
    (⋃₀ {s : Set G | ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ IsRNBarGroup N ∧ (N : Set G) = s})

instance rnBarRadical_normal (G : Type*) [Group G] : (rnBarRadical G).Normal :=
  Subgroup.normalClosure_normal

/-- Is the property $\overline{RN}$ radical? That is, for every group $G$, is the subgroup
generated by all normal $\overline{RN}$-subgroups of $G$ itself an $\overline{RN}$-group? -/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem parts.a : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsRNBarGroup (rnBarRadical G) := by
  sorry

/-- Is the property $\overline{RN}$ strongly radical? That is, is it radical and, for every group
$G$, does $G/\overline{RN}(G)$ have no nontrivial normal $\overline{RN}$-subgroups? -/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem parts.a.variants.strongly_radical : answer(sorry) ↔
    (∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsRNBarGroup (rnBarRadical G)) ∧
    (∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (N : Subgroup (G ⧸ rnBarRadical G)),
      N.Normal → IsRNBarGroup N → N = ⊥) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«2.22»
modeling_decisions: A complete normal system is represented by a set of subgroups that is linearly ordered by inclusion and closed under arbitrary subgroup suprema and infima; closure for the empty subfamily ensures that the trivial and whole subgroups occur.
A successor factor in a system is represented by a jump: two members A < B with no member of the system strictly between them.
Normality at a jump A < B is expressed by normality of A.comap B.subtype in B.

The factor B/A is abelian exactly when the ambient subgroup commutator ⁅B, B⁆ is contained in A; this avoids introducing quotient types inside the system predicate while retaining the intended factor condition.
A refinement is inclusion of the underlying complete subgroup chains.

The radical candidate is defined as the normal closure of the union of all normal RN-bar subgroups. Since every subgroup in that union is normal, this equals the subgroup generated by them and gives a canonical normality instance for the quotient.

Strong radicality is stated as the conjunction of radicality and the assertion that every normal RN-bar subgroup of the quotient is bottom, because the source defines strongly radical only for an already radical property.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 2.22

by Sh. S. Kemkhadze

a) An abstract group-theoretic property $\Sigma$ is said to be *radical (in our sense)* if,
in any group $G$, the subgroup $\Sigma(G)$ generated by all normal $\Sigma$-subgroups is a
$\Sigma$-subgroup itself (called the *$\Sigma$-radical* of $G$). A radical property $\Sigma$
is said to be *strongly radical* if, for any group $G$, the factor-group $G/\Sigma(G)$
contains no non-trivial normal $\Sigma$-subgroups. Is the property $\overline{RN}$ radical?
strongly radical?

Here $\overline{RN}$ is the class of Kurosh and Chernikov: a *normal system* of a group $G$
is a complete chain of subgroups of $G$ (containing $1$ and $G$, linearly ordered by
inclusion, and closed under unions and intersections) in which every member is normal in
its immediate successor; a normal system is *solvable* if all of its factors $B/A$
(for jumps $A \subset B$ of the system) are abelian. A group is an *$RN$-group* if it has a
solvable normal system, and an *$\overline{RN}$-group* if every normal system of the group
can be refined to a solvable normal system.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 2.22
- A. G. Kurosh, S. N. Chernikov, *Solvable and nilpotent groups*, Uspekhi Mat. Nauk 2 (1947),
  no. 3, 18–59 (the classes $RN$ and $\overline{RN}$)
- A. G. Kurosh, *The Theory of Groups*, Vol. II, Chelsea, 1960 (normal systems and
  generalized solvable groups)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«2.22»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- `IsJump 𝒮 A B` says that `A` and `B` are members of the set `𝒮` of subgroups with
`A < B` and no member of `𝒮` strictly between them, i.e. `B` immediately follows `A` in `𝒮`.
The quotient $B/A$ is then a *factor* of `𝒮`. -/
def IsJump (𝒮 : Set (Subgroup G)) (A B : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  A ∈ 𝒮 ∧ B ∈ 𝒮 ∧ A < B ∧ ∀ C ∈ 𝒮, ¬ (A < C ∧ C < B)

/-- A *normal system* of a group $G$ (in the sense of Kurosh) is a set `𝒮` of subgroups of
$G$ which is linearly ordered by inclusion, complete (closed under suprema and infima of
arbitrary subsets; in particular `⊥ = sSup ∅` and `⊤ = sInf ∅` belong to `𝒮`), and such that
every member is a normal subgroup of the member immediately following it. -/
structure IsNormalSystem (𝒮 : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop where
  isChain : IsChain (· ≤ ·) 𝒮
  sSup_mem : ∀ 𝒯 ⊆ 𝒮, sSup 𝒯 ∈ 𝒮
  sInf_mem : ∀ 𝒯 ⊆ 𝒮, sInf 𝒯 ∈ 𝒮
  normal_of_isJump : ∀ A B, IsJump 𝒮 A B → (A.subgroupOf B).Normal

/-- A system `𝒮` of subgroups is *solvable* if all of its factors are abelian, i.e. for every
jump `A < B` of `𝒮` the quotient $B/A$ is abelian: $[B, B] \le A$. -/
def IsSolvableSystem (𝒮 : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop :=
  ∀ A B, IsJump 𝒮 A B → ⁅B, B⁆ ≤ A

/-- A group $G$ is an *$\overline{RN}$-group* (Kurosh–Chernikov) if every normal system of $G$
can be refined to a solvable normal system, i.e. is contained in a solvable normal system. -/
def IsRNBarGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ 𝒮 : Set (Subgroup G), IsNormalSystem 𝒮 →
    ∃ 𝒯 : Set (Subgroup G), 𝒮 ⊆ 𝒯 ∧ IsNormalSystem 𝒯 ∧ IsSolvableSystem 𝒯

/-- The subgroup $\overline{RN}(G)$ of a group $G$ generated by all normal
$\overline{RN}$-subgroups of $G$ (the $\overline{RN}$-radical of $G$ in Kemkhadze's sense). -/
def rnBarRadical (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  sSup {H : Subgroup G | H.Normal ∧ IsRNBarGroup H}

open scoped Pointwise in
/-- The subgroup generated by a set of normal subgroups is normal. -/
theorem normal_sSup {S : Set (Subgroup G)} (hS : ∀ H ∈ S, H.Normal) :
    (sSup S).Normal := by
  refine ⟨fun n hn g => ?_⟩
  have h : MulAut.conj g • sSup S ≤ sSup S := by
    rw [Subgroup.pointwise_smul_def, Subgroup.map_le_iff_le_comap]
    refine sSup_le fun H hH => ?_
    have := hS H hH
    rw [← Subgroup.map_le_iff_le_comap, ← Subgroup.pointwise_smul_def,
      Subgroup.Normal.conj_smul_eq_self]
    exact le_sSup hH
  exact h (Subgroup.smul_mem_pointwise_smul n (MulAut.conj g) _ hn)

instance rnBarRadical_normal : (rnBarRadical G).Normal :=
  normal_sSup fun _ hH => hH.1

/-- The system `{⊥, ⊤}` consisting of the trivial subgroup and the whole group is a normal
system of every group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isNormalSystem_pair : IsNormalSystem ({⊥, ⊤} : Set (Subgroup G)) where
  isChain := IsChain.pair bot_le
  sSup_mem 𝒯 h𝒯 := by
    by_cases h : ⊤ ∈ 𝒯
    · exact Or.inr (top_le_iff.1 (le_sSup h))
    · refine Or.inl (sSup_eq_bot.2 fun A hA => ?_)
      rcases h𝒯 hA with rfl | rfl
      · rfl
      · exact absurd hA h
  sInf_mem 𝒯 h𝒯 := by
    by_cases h : ⊥ ∈ 𝒯
    · exact Or.inl (le_bot_iff.1 (sInf_le h))
    · refine Or.inr (sInf_eq_top.2 fun A hA => ?_)
      rcases h𝒯 hA with rfl | rfl
      · exact absurd hA h
      · rfl
  normal_of_isJump A B := by
    rintro ⟨hA, -, hAB, -⟩
    rcases hA with rfl | rfl
    · rw [Subgroup.bot_subgroupOf]
      infer_instance
    · exact absurd hAB not_top_lt

/-- Every abelian group is an $\overline{RN}$-group: all factors of any normal system of an
abelian group are abelian. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsRNBarGroup.of_isMulCommutative [IsMulCommutative G] : IsRNBarGroup G :=
  fun 𝒮 h𝒮 => ⟨𝒮, subset_rfl, h𝒮, fun A _ _ => Subgroup.commutator_le.2 fun x _ y _ => by
    rw [commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm.2 (IsMulCommutative.is_comm.comm x y)]
    exact A.one_mem⟩

/--
Is the property $\overline{RN}$ radical? That is, is it true that for every group $G$ the
subgroup $\overline{RN}(G)$ generated by all normal $\overline{RN}$-subgroups of $G$ is itself
an $\overline{RN}$-group?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«2.22».parts.a : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsRNBarGroup (rnBarRadical G) := by
  sorry

Is the property $\overline{RN}$ strongly radical? That is, is it true that $\overline{RN}$ is
radical (for every group $G$ the subgroup $\overline{RN}(G)$ generated by all normal
$\overline{RN}$-subgroups of $G$ is an $\overline{RN}$-group) and, moreover, for every group

    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (K : Subgroup (G ⧸ rnBarRadical G)),

The table's reading (part a = 'is RN-bar radical?', variant = 'is RN-bar strongly radical?' as a conjunction with radicality) matches the statement's own definitions. Minor remark on the notes: 'every serial section B/A is an RN-group' should be understood for pairs A ◁ B lying in a common normal system (e.g. jumps); I used the primary Kurosh–Chernikov definition instead, so nothing hinges on this.
modeling_decisions: RN-bar is formalized by Kurosh–Chernikov's primary definition ('every normal system can be refined to a solvable normal system'), not by the equivalent 'every serial factor is an RN-group' reformulation mentioned in the table notes; the two are equivalent by a routine argument but the primary definition is the one in the sources.

A normal system is modeled as a set 𝒮 of subgroups with `IsChain (· ≤ ·) 𝒮`, closure under `sSup`/`sInf` of all subsets (so ⊥ = sSup ∅ and ⊤ = sInf ∅ are automatically members, matching 'contains E and G'), and `(A.subgroupOf B).Normal` for every jump (A, B). For a chain of subgroups `sSup` of a nonempty subset is the set-theoretic union, so this is Kurosh's completeness.
'Refinement' is modeled as set inclusion 𝒮 ⊆ 𝒯 of systems, following Kurosh.
'Solvable normal system' (all factors abelian) is expressed as ⁅B, B⁆ ≤ A for every jump (A, B), avoiding the need for a quotient group; this is equivalent to B/A being abelian when A ◁ B.

A 'Σ-subgroup' H ≤ G is modeled as `IsRNBarGroup ↥H` (H regarded as an abstract group); the definition is intrinsic, hence isomorphism-invariant, as required for an 'abstract group-theoretic property'.
Σ(G) is `sSup` of the set of normal RN-bar subgroups. The set always contains ⊥ (the trivial group is RN-bar), and in any case `sSup ∅ = ⊥`, so no empty-join issue arises.
Groups are quantified as `G : Type` (universe 0), following the other Kourovka files (1.40, 1.74, 19.25, 20.76).

The strongly-radical slot is the conjunction (radical) ∧ (no non-trivial normal RN-bar subgroup of G/Σ(G)), as prescribed by the decomposition table since the statement's definition presupposes radicality.

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

  top_mem : ⊤ ∈ 𝒮

by Sh. S. Kemkhadze

all normal subgroups with the property again has the property. It is strongly
radical if it is radical and the corresponding quotient has no non-trivial
normal subgroup with the property. Problem 2.22 asks whether Kurosh's class
$\overline{RN}$ is radical, and whether it is strongly radical.

Here $\overline{RN}$ is the class of groups in which every complete normal
system can be refined to a solvable normal system, one whose factors are
abelian.

namespace Kourovka.«2.22»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A complete chain of subgroups contains the infimum and supremum of each
of its subfamilies. In particular, it contains both the trivial subgroup and
the whole group. -/
def IsCompleteSubgroupChain (S : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop :=
  IsChain (· ≤ ·) S ∧
    ∀ T : Set (Subgroup G), T ⊆ S → sInf T ∈ S ∧ sSup T ∈ S

/-- The pair $A < B$ is a factor (jump) of the chain $S$ if no member of $S$
lies strictly between $A$ and $B$. -/
def IsChainFactor (S : Set (Subgroup G)) (A B : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  A ∈ S ∧ B ∈ S ∧ A < B ∧
    ∀ C ∈ S, ¬(A < C ∧ C < B)

/-- A complete subgroup chain is a normal system if the lower subgroup in
every factor is normal in the upper subgroup. -/
def IsNormalSystem (S : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop :=
  IsCompleteSubgroupChain S ∧
    ∀ ⦃A B : Subgroup G⦄, IsChainFactor S A B → B ≤ A.normalizer

/-- A normal system is solvable if all of its factors are abelian. The
condition $[B,B] \le A$ says that the factor $B/A$ is abelian. -/
def IsSolvableNormalSystem (S : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop :=
  IsNormalSystem S ∧
    ∀ ⦃A B : Subgroup G⦄, IsChainFactor S A B → ⁅B, B⁆ ≤ A

complete normal system has a refinement that is a solvable normal system. -/
def IsRNBarGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Set (Subgroup G), IsNormalSystem S →
    ∃ T : Set (Subgroup G), S ⊆ T ∧ IsSolvableNormalSystem T

$\overline{RN}$-subgroups. -/

  sSup {H : Subgroup G | H.Normal ∧ IsRNBarGroup H}

    (fun H : {H : Subgroup G // H.Normal ∧ IsRNBarGroup H} => H.1)

solvable normal system. (In Robinson's terminology, a normal system is a *series*.)

  top_mem : ⊤ ∈ S

/-- A complete chain of subgroups. Completeness means closure under arbitrary infima and
suprema; in particular, the chain contains both the trivial and the whole subgroup. -/
structure CompleteSubgroupChain (G : Type*) [Group G] where
  /-- The complete sublattice underlying the chain. -/
  toCompleteSublattice : CompleteSublattice (Subgroup G)
  /-- Any two terms in the system are comparable. -/
  isChain' : IsChain (· ≤ ·) (toCompleteSublattice : Set (Subgroup G))

namespace CompleteSubgroupChain

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

instance : SetLike (CompleteSubgroupChain G) (Subgroup G) where
  coe S := S.toCompleteSublattice
  coe_injective' S T h := by
    cases S
    cases T
    simp_all

/-- The successor of $H$ in a complete subgroup chain is the intersection of all terms
strictly above $H$. At the top term this is again the top term. -/
def successor (S : CompleteSubgroupChain G) (H : Subgroup G) : Subgroup G :=
  sInf {K : Subgroup G | K ∈ S ∧ H < K}

end CompleteSubgroupChain

/-- A normal system in a group is a complete chain of subgroups in which each term is
normal in its successor. -/
structure NormalSystem (G : Type*) [Group G] extends CompleteSubgroupChain G where
  /-- Each term is contained in, and normal as a subgroup of, its successor. -/
  normal_successor' : ∀ H : Subgroup G, H ∈ toCompleteSublattice →
    H ≤ toCompleteSubgroupChain.successor H ∧
      (H.subgroupOf (toCompleteSubgroupChain.successor H)).Normal

namespace NormalSystem

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A normal system `T` refines a normal system `S` when every term of `S` is a term of
`T`. -/
def Refines (T S : NormalSystem G) : Prop :=
  (S.toCompleteSublattice : Set (Subgroup G)) ⊆ T.toCompleteSublattice

/-- A normal system is solvable when all of its factors are abelian. The factor above
$H$ is abelian exactly when every commutator of elements of the successor of $H$ lies
in $H$. -/
def IsSolvable (S : NormalSystem G) : Prop :=
  ∀ (H : Subgroup G), H ∈ S.toCompleteSublattice →
    ∀ x y : S.toCompleteSubgroupChain.successor H, ⁅(x : G), (y : G)⁆ ∈ H

end NormalSystem

that is a solvable normal system. -/

$\overline{RN}$-subgroups. The normal closure gives this generated subgroup a canonical
normality instance; it does not enlarge it, since all the subgroups in the union are normal. -/

in any group $G$, the subgroup $\Sigma(G)$ generated by all normal $\Sigma$-subgroups is a
$\Sigma$-subgroup itself (called the *$\Sigma$-radical* of $G$). A radical property $\Sigma$

$\overline{RN}$-group if every normal system of $G$ can be refined to a solvable normal
system. A *normal system* of $G$ (Kurosh) is a set of subgroups of $G$ that contains $1$
and $G$, is linearly ordered by inclusion, is complete (closed under unions and
intersections of arbitrary subsets), and is such that $A$ is a normal subgroup of $B$ for
every jump $A \subset B$ (a pair of members of the system with no member strictly between
them). The *factors* of the system are the quotients $B/A$ over the jumps, and the system is
*solvable* if all its factors are abelian. A *refinement* of a normal system is a normal
system containing it.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)

*Reference:* A. G. Kurosh, *The Theory of Groups*, Vol. II, Chapter XIV (normal systems,
$RN$- and $\overline{RN}$-groups).

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- `(A, B)` is a *jump* of a set `S` of subgroups of `G`: `A` and `B` are members of `S`
with `A < B`, and no member of `S` lies strictly between `A` and `B`. -/
def IsJump (S : Set (Subgroup G)) (A B : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  A ∈ S ∧ B ∈ S ∧ A < B ∧ ∀ C ∈ S, ¬ (A < C ∧ C < B)

/-- A *normal system* of `G` in the sense of Kurosh: a set `S` of subgroups of `G` that
contains `⊥` and `⊤`, is linearly ordered by inclusion, is complete (the union and the
intersection of any subset of `S` belong to `S`), and is such that `A` is a normal subgroup
of `B` for every jump `(A, B)` of `S`. -/
structure IsNormalSystem (S : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop where
  bot_mem : ⊥ ∈ S
  top_mem : ⊤ ∈ S
  isChain : IsChain (· ≤ ·) S
  sSup_mem : ∀ T ⊆ S, sSup T ∈ S
  sInf_mem : ∀ T ⊆ S, sInf T ∈ S

/-- A *solvable normal system* of `G`: a normal system all of whose factors `B / A`
(over the jumps `(A, B)`) are abelian, i.e. `⁅x, y⁆ ∈ A` for all `x, y ∈ B`. -/
def IsSolvableNormalSystem (S : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop :=
  IsNormalSystem S ∧ ∀ A B, IsJump S A B → ∀ x ∈ B, ∀ y ∈ B, ⁅x, y⁆ ∈ A

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 2.22

by Sh. S. Kemkhadze

Is Kurosh's group-theoretic property $\overline{RN}$ radical? Is it strongly radical?

A group has property $\overline{RN}$ if every complete normal system can be refined to a
solvable normal system. A complete normal system is a complete chain of subgroups in which each
subgroup is normal in its successor. It is solvable when all of its factors are abelian.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«2.22»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A set of subgroups is a complete chain if it is linearly ordered by inclusion and contains
the infimum and supremum of each of its subsets. In particular, by taking the empty subset, it
contains the trivial and whole subgroups. -/
def IsCompleteSubgroupChain (S : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop :=
  IsChain (· ≤ ·) S ∧
    ∀ T : Set (Subgroup G), T ⊆ S → sInf T ∈ S ∧ sSup T ∈ S

/-- In a chain `S`, the subgroup `K` is a successor of `H` if both belong to `S`, $H<K$, and no
member of `S` lies strictly between them. -/
def IsSuccessorIn (S : Set (Subgroup G)) (H K : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  H ∈ S ∧ K ∈ S ∧ H < K ∧ ∀ L ∈ S, ¬(H < L ∧ L < K)

/-- A complete normal system of a group is a complete chain of subgroups in which each subgroup
is normal in its successor. Normality here is internal to the successor subgroup. -/
def IsNormalSystem (S : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop :=
  IsCompleteSubgroupChain S ∧
    ∀ H K : Subgroup G, IsSuccessorIn S H K → (H.subgroupOf K).Normal

/-- A solvable normal system is a complete normal system whose factors are abelian. For a
successive pair $H<K$, abelianness of $K/H$ is expressed as $[K,K]\leq H$. -/
def IsSolvableNormalSystem (S : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop :=
  IsNormalSystem S ∧
    ∀ H K : Subgroup G, IsSuccessorIn S H K → ⁅K, K⁆ ≤ H

/-- Kurosh's property $\overline{RN}$: every complete normal system has a solvable normal-system
refinement. A refinement contains every member of the original system. -/
def IsRNBarGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Set (Subgroup G), IsNormalSystem S →
    ∃ T : Set (Subgroup G), IsSolvableNormalSystem T ∧ S ⊆ T

/-- The $\overline{RN}$-radical candidate of `G`, generated by all normal $\overline{RN}$
subgroups. Since all the generating subgroups are normal, their normal closure agrees with the
subgroup generated by them. -/
def rnBarRadical (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.normalClosure
    (⋃ H : {H : Subgroup G // H.Normal ∧ IsRNBarGroup H}, (H : Set G))

/-- The $\overline{RN}$-radical candidate is normal, since it is defined as a normal closure. -/
instance rnBarRadical_normal (G : Type*) [Group G] : (rnBarRadical G).Normal := by
  unfold rnBarRadical
  infer_instance

/--
Is the property $\overline{RN}$ radical? That is, for every group $G$, is the subgroup generated
by all normal $\overline{RN}$-subgroups of $G$ itself an $\overline{RN}$-group?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem parts.a : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsRNBarGroup (rnBarRadical G) := by
  sorry

Is the property $\overline{RN}$ strongly radical? By definition this asks both whether it is
radical and whether, for every group $G$, the quotient by its $\overline{RN}$-radical contains no
nontrivial normal $\overline{RN}$-subgroup.
-/

theorem parts.a.variants.strongly_radical : answer(sorry) ↔
    (∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsRNBarGroup (rnBarRadical G)) ∧
    (∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (H : Subgroup (G ⧸ rnBarRadical G)),
      H.Normal → IsRNBarGroup H → H = ⊥) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«2.22»
modeling_decisions: A complete chain is represented as a set of subgroups linearly ordered by inclusion and closed under the infimum and supremum of every subset; closure for the empty subset ensures that the trivial and whole subgroups occur.
A successor pair means two members of the chain with strict inclusion and no chain member strictly between them. Normality is internal to the upper subgroup via `(H.subgroupOf K).Normal`.
An abelian factor K/H is represented by the equivalent commutator condition `⁅K, K⁆ ≤ H` on a successor pair.
A refinement is represented by inclusion of the original set of subgroups in the refining set.

The radical candidate is expressed as the normal closure of the union of all normal RN-bar subgroups. Since the indexed subgroups are all normal, this equals the subgroup generated by them and directly exposes normality for the quotient.
Strong radicality is stated as a conjunction because the source defines strongly radical only for a radical property.
